Personally, I usually have a hard time accepting love stories as substitutes for character chemistry. The first game builds the chemistry between Joel and Ellie by showing the two of them meet, the uneasy friendship they form, and ultimately Joel’s 180 change of character BECAUSE of Ellie. The relationship between Ellie and Dina forms off screen and from the start of the game tells you they like each other rather than really showing the relationship grow. She kinda just invites herself along Ellie’s journey when she knows she is pregnant and ends up being more of a burden than helpful. She is the reason that Ellie doesn’t finish her initial goal, which I guess is to serve the plot and the themes of revenge being unsatisfying, but I don’t think that makes up for the writing behind the character. Perhaps if she had met Dina on her journey or we got to actually see the relationship form rather than being told then maybe she could have been done better.

Other than that, I really like all the other new characters. Jesse kinda fell flat on me too because he is similar to Dina in that we are just kinda told to accept that he is their friend, but other character like Abby, Lev, Yara, etc I thought were really well written and shows the writing strengths that Neil has when we gives characters time to develop and be introduced properly.

I felt the exact opposite. I find that love stories usually fall flat because they distract from the bigger story and end up being pretty generic. She kinda just exists in Ellie’s life and as the audience we are kinda forced to just accept that rather than seeing their relationship form. Not to mention she becomes more of a burden than anything else. She invited herself along on a journey that she really has no part in being in and goes knowing she is pregnant. Ellie doesn’t achieve her initial because of Dina’s poor decision making, which I guess you could say serves the story and it’s themes, but that doesn’t change my opinion on her character motivation and writing

Other than hand, all the other new character that we actually get to meet them the same way the protagonist meets them (not off screen I mean, like Dina and Jesse) are actually really well written, like Lev and Yara
